missing_info: pyproject.toml declaration of redis (any version specifier or constraint on redis or hiredis)
uv.lock or the output of uv lock/uv sync showing the resolved redis version and why 2.0.0 was chosen
exact command and full output of uv sync (with -v if possible)
Python index/registry configuration (index URL, any mirror or private index that might only carry old redis releases)
whether the environment was fresh (no existing .venv or lock) and whether the issue reproduces on a second machine
escalation_reason: Torn between question and bug: the reporter labels it a bug, but the resolved version 2.0.0 is only explained by a constraint or index issue in the reporter's project, which cannot be checked from the report. A maintainer should confirm whether a resolver defect is involved.
rationale: The report says uv sync always installs redis 2.0.0 for redis[hiredis]. get_package_metadata shows the current redis release is 8.1.0 (requires_python >=3.10, hiredis extra present), so picking 2.0.0 with no version pin is unexpected and points to a constraint in the project (pyproject, lock file or index) rather than a clear uv defect. The report gives no pyproject, lock, exact command or output, so it cannot be reproduced. No duplicate issues were found by search_issues. Playbook rule 6 (rule out config mistakes first) favours question, but the missing evidence leaves a bug call possible, so this is low confidence and escalated.
